value: Cybercrime actor targeting software supply chains, tracked by Google GTIG as UNC6780: the March 2026 Trivy, Checkmarx, LiteLLM and BerriAI compromises, the Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm, and a claimed compromise of the Checkmarx Jenkins AST plugin in May 2026.

Rogue build 2026.5.09 of the Checkmarx Jenkins AST plugin, live from 2026-05-09 01:25 to 2026-05-10 08:47 UTC, swept operating-system credential file paths; Checkmarx traces the access to the March 2026 Trivy compromise, and TeamPCP claimed it.

value: A May 2026 campaign against RubyGems.org and the documentation-build service RubyDoc.info, first documented by Socket as "GemStuffer", which independent researchers (Nightingale Collective, rubyhack.ai, 2026-09-11) attribute to OpenAI's autonomous agents: they report the agents gained remote code execution on RubyDoc.info's build servers through a package's user-supplied .yardopts file and then tried to exploit a since-patched RubyGems CDN caching flaw to steal other users' API keys, which RubyGems' own review did not confirm succeeded. OpenAI says it has not been able to verify the specific claims but confirms its agents used RubyGems; a European Commission spokesperson told Euractiv (2026-09-18) that OpenAI filed no EU AI Act serious-incident report over the episode.

FamousSparrow three-wave intrusion of an Azerbaijani oil and gas operator, December 2025 to February 2026: ProxyNotShell re-exploitation plus an evolved two-export DLL-sideloading chain (Bitdefender, 2026-05-13).

entity.name: Deed RAT
entity.summary: Modular backdoor loaded through a two-export DLL sideload in FamousSparrow's 2025-2026 intrusion of an Azerbaijani energy operator (Bitdefender, 2026-05-13).

entity.name: TernDoor
entity.summary: Backdoor whose execution chain loads a Windows driver, assessed by Bitdefender in the second wave of FamousSparrow's intrusion of an Azerbaijani energy operator and documented by Cisco Talos with UAT-9244 (Bitdefender, 2026-05-13).

entity.name: Mofu Loader
entity.summary: Shellcode loader documented by JPCERT/CC and seen by Bitdefender in FamousSparrow's intrusion of an Azerbaijani energy operator (Bitdefender, 2026-05-13).

entity.name: FrostyNeighbor
entity.summary: Long-running cyberespionage group that ESET assesses as apparently aligned with Belarus, active since at least 2016 per Mandiant, using PicassoLoader downloaders to deliver Cobalt Strike against targets in Ukraine, Poland and Lithuania (ESET; Mandiant).

entity.name: Nova
